plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large daisy-like flower heads made of a dark central disc surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. The heads track the sun during early growth and are widely grown as ornamentals and for seeds and oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide, including the US Great Plains, Ukraine, Russia, and France
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of up to 2,000 tiny florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August, with late blooms in cooler climates into September
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the Pacific Northwest of the US
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', since the Romans used it to scent baths.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower forming dense colonies with arching plumes of tiny golden-yellow flower heads. It is an important late-summer nectar and pollen source for native bees, butterflies, and migrating monarchs.
plants.location: Native to meadows, roadsides, and prairies of eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and insect-carried; ragweed, which blooms at the same time, is the real culprit.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A large evergreen shrub producing spectacular crimson flower heads up to 15 cm across, surrounded by showy red bracts. Each head is made of hundreds of small tubular flowers and is rich in nectar for honeyeater birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August to November)
plants.location: Native to the sandstone ridges and forests of southeastern New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales, and its name comes from an Aboriginal word meaning 'seen from afar'.
